instructions: Start with the dressing. Mince the 1 garlic clove and squeeze the lime. You want about 2 tbsp of juice.

Put the garlic and lime juice in a jar with 1/4 cup fish sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1/4 cup vegetable oil and 1 tbsp sugar. Put the lid on and shake it until the sugar has dissolved, then leave it on the counter while you cut the vegetables.
Cut the cabbage in half and shred one half as finely as you can, about 6 cups. Slice half the red onion paper thin.
Seed the bell pepper and cut it into thin strips. Halve the 2 cucumbers lengthwise, scoop out the seeds with a teaspoon and slice them into thin half moons.
Peel 1 large carrot and cut it into thin matchsticks, or shred it on the big holes of a box grater.
Pick about 1 cup of mint leaves and 1 cup of cilantro leaves, packed. Tear any big mint leaves in half.
Cut or pull the 12 oz chicken into thin strips about the size of the carrot pieces.
Finely chop the 1/2 cup peanuts. Thinly slice the chilli and put it in a small bowl for the table.
Put the cabbage, onion, pepper, cucumbers, carrot, herbs and chicken in your biggest bowl. Shake the dressing again, pour in half and toss well with your hands or tongs.
Leave it for 5 minutes, so the cabbage softens a little. Toss again and pour in most of the rest of the dressing.
Taste a forkful. If it's flat, add the last of the dressing. If you're packing it for lunch, keep the peanuts in a separate container and scatter them on just before eating.
Scatter the peanuts over the top. Serve with the sliced chilli on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions toss shredded cabbage, onion, mint, cilantro and chicken with a fish sauce, lime, sugar and garlic dressing. RecipeTin Eats, the lead, starts from cooked chicken, adds bell pepper, cucumber and carrot, uses a dressing with rice vinegar and oil, and dresses it in two goes with a 5 minute rest so the cabbage softens, finishing with lots of chopped peanuts. Takes Two Eggs and I Am a Food Blog poach the chicken first (with ginger and onion, or scallion and ginger), use green cabbage and an oil-free nuoc cham style dressing; Takes Two Eggs adds rau ram and fried shallots and I Am a Food Blog tops it with avocado. This one keeps the chilli on the side instead of in the dressing.
